facts.fact: The World Bank study says that since 2016 civil registration is carried out by civil registration officers at sector level, who report birth and death data electronically to the National Identification Agency (NIDA) for a record to be created or flagged in the National Population Register.

The World Bank study says that since 2016 all local departments issuing birth certificates make direct digital entries in the NIDA system, and that sector civil registration officers report birth and death data electronically to NIDA.
The World Bank study says that since 2016 all local departments issuing birth certificates make direct digital entries in the NIDA system, at sector level, and gives no count of the offices.

The World Bank study says the National Identification Agency, a permanent government agency since 2011, holds the system into which sector civil registration officers have entered birth and death data since 2016.

The World Bank study, researched in 2017, says Rwanda is embarking on a CRVS Information Management System for timely digital recording of births, deaths, marriages, divorces, adoptions and guardianship and nationality, needing 1,000 to 1,100 touch points, after a feasibility study by the consultant PBLQ; this is a system being started, not one in use.
